Various types of electronics sit on a shelf at the Internet Archive offices in San Francisco on March 24, 2023. The Internet Archive, thanks to its designation by California Sen. Alex Padilla, joins a network of over 1,100 libraries that make government documents accessible to the public.
(Beth LaBerge/KQED)
The San Francisco-based
Internet Archive
now has federal depository status, joining a network of over 1,100 libraries that archive government documents and make them accessible to the public — even as ongoing legal challenges pose an existential threat to the organization.
California Sen. Alex Padilla made the designation in
a letter
sent Thursday to the Government Publishing Office, which
oversees the program
. In the letter, shared exclusively with KQED, Padilla praised the Internet Archive for its “digital focus” and said it “is leading the way when it comes to providing online library services.”
“The Archive’s digital-first approach makes it the perfect fit for a modern federal depository library, expanding access to federal government publications amid an increasingly digital landscape,” Padilla said in a statement to KQED. “The Internet Archive has broken down countless barriers to accessing information, and it is my honor to provide this designation to help further their mission of providing ‘Universal Access to All Knowledge.’”
Sponsored
Under federal law, members of Congress can designate up to two qualified libraries for federal depository status.
Internet Archive founder Brewster Kahle said that while the nonprofit organization has always functioned as a library, this new designation makes it easier to work with the other federal depository libraries. That, he said, is a service to everyone.
Brewster Kahle closes a storage container with books from the Allen County Public Library at an Internet Archive storage facility in Richmond on March 30.
(Beth LaBerge/KQED)
“ I think there is a great deal of excitement to have an organization such as the Internet Archive, which has physical collections of materials, but is really known mostly for being accessible as part of the internet,” Kahle said. “And helping integrate these materials into things like Wikipedia, so that the whole internet ecosystem gets stronger as digital learners get closer access into the government materials.”
The Federal Depository Library Program was established by Congress in 1813, with the intention of ensuring that government records would be accessible to the American public. It includes maps, environmental reports, health studies, congressional records, newspapers and books.
These records account for “millions and millions of pages” that can take up entire floors of public libraries, Kahle said. San Diego’s public library
gave up its federal depository status
in 2020 because its government documents took up so much space and often went unused.
While documents stored on microfiche or microfilm are easy to copy, they aren’t easy to access. The GPO has been moving toward digital preservation since 2016 and runs an
online database
of government records, and in recent years, it has
ramped up efforts
to digitize the Federal Depository Library Program.
Participating libraries have largely pivoted to the GPO’s digital approach, but digitizing countless physical documents is a massive undertaking — one that the Internet Archive has experience with.
For years, the Internet Archive has helped libraries and other academic institutions in digitizing their collections and hosting them online. In 2022, it launched
Democracy’s Library
, a free online compendium of government research and publications.
Joining the Federal Depository Library Program is the next step in the evolution of Democracy’s Library, Kahle said. The Archive is “just doing what it’s always been doing,” but now, it’s more convenient.
“By being part of the program itself, it just gets us closer to the source of where the materials are coming from, so that it’s more reliably delivered to the Internet Archive, to then be made available to the patrons of the Internet Archive or partner libraries,” he continued.
Laura Gibbs looks at memorabilia at the Internet Archive offices in San Francisco.
(Beth LaBerge/KQED)
The organization has faced legal challenges over some of its archival practices. Its Open Library was at the center of a yearslong
legal battle
after four major publishers sued the Internet Archive for
temporarily lifting its waitlists
in 2020 — instead of loaning its digital copies to one user at a time. By doing so, the publishers alleged, the Internet Archive illegally provided free e-books.
Last year, an appeals court upheld a 2023 federal court decision that ruled against the Internet Archive. The organization has had to remove more than half a million titles

data.author: ulrischa
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了新发现的星际天体3I/ATLAS，这是一颗被认为可能来自遥远星系的大型彗星，迅速成为天文界的焦点。科学家正抓紧时间利用最佳仪器研究这个快速穿越太阳系的物体。初步数据显示，3I/ATLAS很可能是一颗由天然过程形成的古老彗星，直径约1.2公里，年龄可追溯至70亿年前。尽管有研究（如哈佛大学天文学家Abraham Loeb的论文）提出其可能是外星技术的假设，但主流观点和现有证据表明，它只是一颗自然形成的彗星。文章还提到，历史上多次有天文学家误将未知天体现象误认为外星信号，提醒读者在面对未知时应保持科学审慎态度。

The team is essentially flagging 3I/ATLAS as a candidate for alien technology and, perhaps alarmingly, as something that might actually pose an existential threat to humanity. Sounds absolutely bonkers, but itâs a topic worth exploring and not something to reflexively toss onto the garbage heap.
Almost certainly a comet
From the moment it entered our view, 3I/ATLASâthe third interstellar object ever detected in our solar systemâinstantly became the biggest news in astronomy for the month, if not the year. Astronomers are using the rare opportunity to study the object in as much detail as possible using the best instruments available. A
clear picture
of the object is emerging, suggesting itâs very likely an
enormous, icy comet
thatâs
considerably older
than our solar system;
preliminary estimates suggest it’s 0.74 miles long (1.2 kilometers) and dates back some 7 billion years.Â
An Interstellar Comet Is Here, and Its Age Is Mind-Bending
The interstellar interloper is zipping through our solar system at ludicrous speeds, clocking in at 37 miles (60 kilometers) per second. Its velocity is so extreme that itâll exit our solar system and disappear from our view later this year, escaping the gravitational influence of our Sun. Astronomers are therefore under a tight deadline to understand everything they possibly can about 3I/ATLASâan object that originated in some faraway protoplanetary or planetary system.Â
That said, astronomers have already made some great strides in sketching out the finer details of 3I/ATLAS,
quickly churning out papers
pertaining to the visitorâs
age
,
size
, velocity, spin, and, most importantly, its
origin
, based on observational data. According to
research
released earlier this week, the object
is a jumble
of organic molecules, silicates, and carbon-based minerals, placing it in a similar compositional category as asteroids found between Mars and Jupiter.
Animation of 3I/ATLAS, moving through the inner Solar System Â© CSS, D. Rankin
Based on current
data
âmuch of it from researchers working with the newly launched Vera C. Rubin Observatoryâ3I/ATLAS is expected to pass through the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter later this fall, reaching its closest point to the Sun in late October. Excitingly, the Sun’s warmth should sublimate enough ice on the comet to brighten the coma and tail even further.Â
Occam’s comet
Suffice it to say, astronomersâ ongoing investigations into 3I/ATLAS largely confirm that itâs a cometary castaway. Like other comets weâve seen before, 3I/ATLAS likely emerged from natural processes and was banished to interstellar space by some gravitational interaction, such as a close encounter with a gigantic planet or a passing star. Importantly, and despite strange, unfounded claims made in the new Loeb paper, thereâs zero indication that 3I/ATLAS is anything but a natural object formed by natural processes.Â
Yet that hasnât stopped Loeb and his colleagues from venturing beyond the existing evidence. Whatâs more, theyâve violated Occamâs razorâa central tenet of the scientific method. Scientists are told that the simplest explanation is often the best when tackling puzzling phenomena. In this case, the simplest explanation, given the existing evidence, is that 3I/ATLAS is a comet. Often, when astronomers detect something unusual or inexplicable in space, thereâs the urge to invoke extraterrestrial influence.Â
The Many, Many Times Astronomers Mistook Mundane Phenomena for Aliens
This seems to be the case here, but as weâll discuss next, these researchers are not wrong to be asking these sorts of questions. As Sara Webb, an astrophysicist at the Swinburne University of Technology, wrote in
The Conversation
, âObjects like 3I/ATLAS remind us that space is vast, strange, and full of surprises. Most of them have natural explanations. But the strangest objects are worth a
44674239.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了新发现的星际天体3I/ATLAS，这是一颗被认为可能来自遥远星系的大型彗星，迅速成为天文界的焦点。科学家正抓紧时间利用最佳仪器研究这个快速穿越太阳系的物体。初步数据显示，3I/ATLAS很可能是一颗由天然过程形成的古老彗星，直径约1.2公里，年龄可追溯至70亿年前。尽管有研究（如哈佛大学天文学家Abraham Loeb的论文）提出其可能是外星技术的假设，但主流观点和现有证据表明，它只是一颗自然形成的彗星。文章还提到，历史上多次有天文学家误将未知天体现象误认为外星信号，提醒读者在面对未知时应保持科学审慎态度。
44674239.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对哈佛大学天文学家Abraham Loeb及其言论的评价和争议

不同观点：
• **Jtsummers的观点**：  
  - 认为Loeb缺乏实际证据支持其关于外星文明的主张，且多年来一直发表类似言论。
  - 提出两种可能的解释：一种是Loeb发现富人容易被荒谬的说法（如“这是外星人”）吸引并投资，另一种是他已经变成了一个彻底的怪人。
  - 对Loeb及其研究持强烈的负面评价，暗示其言行令哈佛蒙羞。

• **perihelions的观点**：  
  - 同意对Loeb的批评，称其为“寻求关注的 clown”。
  - 提出过去数十亿年中的天体现象（如彗星）也可以被解释为外星探测器，但这种解释并无新意，因为天文学早已预测并观察到类似现象。
  - 认为Loeb的言论只是为了吸引注意力，并质疑其学术贡献。

• **calmbonsai的观点**：  
  - 提醒大家不要从Gizmodo这样的非专业媒体获取天文学信息，暗示该媒体在科学方面的可信度较低。
  - 强调获取准确科学信息的重要性，间接批评了那些依据不可靠来源做出判断的人。

• **giardini的观点**：  
  - 强烈反对在标题中加入“外星科技”这样的字眼，认为这是不负责任的做法。
  - 提出应该停止对相关研究人员的资助，认为他们误导公众。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Abraham Loeb的研究和他关于外星文明的主张是否具有科学依据，以及他是否为了吸引注意力而发表这些言论。
• 不同评论者对Loeb的评价从“缺乏证据”到“寻求关注的小丑”再到“应被剥夺研究资金”，显示出对其言论的强烈不满。
• 对媒体在科学讨论中的角色也有一定关注，尤其是calmbonsai提醒大家注意信息来源的可靠性。

data.title: Wrestling legend Hulk Hogan dies at 71
data.author: nappy-doo
data.article_summary: 摔跤传奇人物浩克·霍根（本名特里·博利亚）于2025年7月24日去世，享年71岁。警方和消防部门证实他因心脏骤停去世。霍根是20世纪80年代职业摔跤热潮的代表人物，被誉为全球知名的流行文化偶像。他以“霍根狂热”时代而闻名，并参演了电影《洛奇3》。近年来，他还涉足右翼政治，并在2024年共和党全国代表大会上公开支持特朗普。此外，霍根曾卷入与Gawker网站的性爱视频官司，最终胜诉并获赔1.4亿美元，导致Gawker破产。

According to the Clearwater Police and Fire departments, Terry Bollea died Thursday morning after a cardiac arrest.
Obituaries

July 24, 2025
1:30 PM ET
Heard on

Andrew Limbong
Wrestling legend Hulk Hogan dies at 71
Audio will be available later today.
Hulk Hogan between matches during WrestleMania in Los Angeles in 2005.
Chris Carlson/AP
hide caption
toggle caption
Chris Carlson/AP
Hulk Hogan, one of the biggest stars of professional wrestling, has died.
The police and fire departments in Clearwater, Florida
,
put out a statement stating they responded to a medical call for a cardiac arrest this morning. Hogan was pronounced dead at a local hospital. He was 71 years old.
Hogan, whose real name is Terry Bollea, was one of the earliest stars of World Wrestling Entertainment and was the face of pro wrestling's boom in popularity during the 1980s.
In a post on X,
the WWE called Hogan "one of pop culture's most recognizable figures," and credits him for helping the brand achieve global recognition.
Sponsor Message
He was so popular, there was a name for his era of popularity – Hulkamania. Hogan parlayed that stardom into movie roles, including a
memorable appearance in
Rocky III
.
More recently, Hogan was a figure of right-wing politics. During the 2024 Republican National Convention,
he spoke on stage, tearing off his shirt to reveal a Trump-Vance shirt
, saying, "Let Trumpamania run wild, brother."
Hogan also became a major figure in the media after the website
Gawker
published a portion of a sex tape of Hogan in 2012. Funded by billionaire Peter Thiel, Hogan sued parent company Gawker Media. Hogan won the lawsuit. A Florida jury awarded him $140 million, driving Gawker Media into bankruptcy.

data.title: Using Radicle CI
data.author: aiw1nt3rs
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何使用Radicle及其持续集成（CI）功能进行软件开发。Radicle通过仓库变更事件支持CI，其CI代理（cib）监听事件并根据配置决定何时运行CI。作者使用自己开发的CI引擎Ambient及相关适配器进行CI操作，并展示了如何在项目中配置和运行CI，包括本地运行和使用容器。作者以一个简单的Rust "hello world"项目为例，演示了从创建Git仓库、编写代码、提交更改到创建Radicle仓库并同步到网络的完整过程。文中还提到Radicle适配器支持多种CI系统，并提供了安装和配置说明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CI系统的适用规模及使用体验优化

不同观点：
• dan_manges 认为CI系统应根据项目规模采用不同方案：
  - 小规模项目：理想情况下可以在本地运行整个CI栈，以避免环境不一致和"只在我的机器上工作"的问题。
  - 大规模项目：由于项目庞大，必须利用远程分布式计算来实现快速反馈（理想情况下在10分钟内完成）。为此，dan_manges 开发了RWX系统，提供多种优化功能，如本地CLI读取工作流定义、远程断点、自动内容缓存、基于图的任务定义等，以提升大规模项目CI系统的使用体验。

• kuehle 强调在服务器上等待CI运行完成并从运行日志中推断问题是非常令人沮丧的。他通过开发"rad-ci"工具来缓解这一问题，主张本地运行CI应更为普遍。

• lbotos 没有直接参与CI系统的讨论，而是对Radicle主页的设计风格表示兴趣，询问是否有一个存档可供参考。

• tough 提到使用"act"工具在本地运行GitHub CI，提供了一种在本地进行CI测试的实际解决方案。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何优化CI系统的使用体验，特别是针对大规模项目。dan_manges 通过开发RWX系统提供了一系列解决方案，而 kuehle 和 tough 则主张通过本地运行CI来提升调试和测试效率。

• 不同的工具和方法被提及，如 dan_manges 的RWX系统、kuehle 的rad-ci、tough 的act，这些工具都旨在解决CI系统使用中的一些痛点，特别是在调试和反馈速度方面。

• lbotos 的评论虽然与CI系统的核心讨论无关，但提到设计风格存档的问题，显示出对设计演变的兴趣。

44658820.article_content:
Using Radicle CI for Development
In this blog post I show how I use Radicle and its CI support for my own software development.
Published by
lars
on 23.07.2025
Overview of Radicle CI
The sample project
CI configuration in the repository
Running CI locally
CI configuration on my CI node
Reporting an issue
Making a change
Installing
Conclusion
In this blog post I show how I use Radicle and its CI support for my
own software development. I show how I start a project, add it to
Radicle, add CI support for it, and manage patches and issues.
I have been working full time on Radicle CI for a couple of years now.
All my personal Git repositories are hosted on Radicle. Radicle CI is
the only CI I now use.
There are instructions to install the software I mention here at the
end.
These days, Iâm not a typical software developer. I usually work in
Emacs and the command line instead of an IDE. In this blog post Iâll
concentrate on the parts of my development process that relate to
Radicle, and not my other tooling.
Overview of Radicle CI
The Radicle node process opens a Unix domain socket to which it sends
events describing changes in the node. One of these events represents
changes to a repository in the nodeâs storage.
Support for CI in Radicle is built around the repository change event.
The Radicle CI broker (
cib
), listens for the events and matches them
against its configuration to decide when to run CI. The node operator
gets to decide for what repositories they run CI.
The CI broker does not itself run CI. It invokes a separate program,
the âadapterâ, which is given the event that triggered CI. The adapter either
executes the run itself, or uses an external CI system to execute it.
This allows Radicle to support a variety of CI systems, by writing a
simple adapter for each.
I have written a CI engine for myself,
Ambient
, and the adapter for that
(
radicle-ci-ambient
), and that is what I use.
There are adapters for running CI locally on the host or in a
container, GitHub actions, Woodpecker, and several others. See
CI
broker
README.md
and
integration
documentation
for a more complete list. The adapter interface is intentionally easy
to implement: it needs to read one line of JSON and write up to two
lines of JSON.
The sample project
This blog post is about Radicle, so Iâm going to use a âhello worldâ
program as an example. This avoids getting mired into the details of
implementing something useful.
First I create a Git repository with a Rust project. I choose Rust,
because I like Rust, but the programming language is irrelevant here.
$ cargo init liw-hello
Creating binary (application) package
... some text removed
$ cd liw-hello
$ git add .
$ git commit -m "chore: cargo init"
[main (root-commit) 5037847] chore: cargo init
3 files changed, 10 insertions(+)
create mode 100644 .gitignore
create mode 100644 Cargo.toml
create mode 100644 src/main.rs
Then I edit the
src/main.rs
file to have some useful content,
including unit tests:
fn main() {
let greeting = Greeting::default()
.greeting("hello")
.whom("world");
println!("{}", greeting.greet());
}
struct Greeting {
greeting: String,
whom: String,
}
impl Default for Greeting {
fn default() -> Self {
Self {
greeting: "howdy".into(),
whom: "partner".into(),
}
}
}
impl Greeting {
fn greeting(mut self, s: &str) -> Self {
self.greeting = s.into();
self
}
fn whom(mut self, s: &str) -> Self {
self.whom = s.into();
self
}
fn greet(&self) -> String {
format!("{} {}", self.greeting, self.whom)
}
}
#[cfg(test)]
mod test {
use super::*;
#[test]
fn default() {
let g = Greeting::default();
assert!(!g.greeting.is_empty());
assert!(!g.whom.is_empty());
}
#[test]
fn sets_greeting() {
let g = Greeting::default().greeting("hi");
assert_eq!(g.greet(), "hi partner");
}
#[test]
fn sets_whom() {
let g = Greeting::default().whom("there");
assert_eq!(g.greet(), "howdy there");
}
}
To commit that, I actually use Emacs with Magit for this, but I also often use
the command line, which I show here.
git commit -am "feat: implement greeting"
Once I have a Git repository with at least one commit, I can create a
Radicle repository for that. I do that on the command line. The
rad
init
command asks the user some questions. The answers could be
provided via option, which is useful for testing, but not something I
usually do when using the program.
$ rad init
Initializing radicle ð¾ repository in /home/liw/radicle/liw-hello..
â Name liw-hello
â Description Sample program for blog post about Radicle and its CI
â Default branch main
â Visibility public
â Repository liw-hello created.
Your Repository ID (RID) is rad:z3dhWQMH8J6nX3Qo97o5oSFMTfgyr.
You can show it any time by running `rad .` from this directory.
â¤ Uploaded to z6MksCgjxU4VZt6qgtZntdikhtXFbsfvKRLPzpKtfCY4rAHR, 0 peer(s) remaining..
â Repository successfully synced to z6MksCgjxU4VZt6qgtZntdikhtXFbsfvKRLPzpKtfCY4rAHR
â Repository successfully synced to 1 node(s).
Your repository has been synced to the network

data.article_summary: 美国空军全球打击司令部宣布暂停使用Sig Sauer M18手枪，此前在怀俄明州F.E. Warren空军基地发生了一起导致21岁空军士兵Brayden Tyriq Lovan死亡的枪击事件。这一决定是在对该武器进行“全面审查”期间做出的。这起死亡事件引发了对M18手枪安全性的再次关注，此前该型号手枪及其民用版P320多次被指控存在意外击发的设计缺陷，并涉及多起诉讼。尽管Sig Sauer否认这些指控，并推动法律修改以保护自己免于承担责任，但美国空军表示将优先考虑人员安全，并在调查期间更换使用其他武器。全面检查将在所有全球打击司令部基地进行，以确定任何直接的安全隐患。

主要讨论点：Sig Sauer P320手枪的意外击发现象及其安全性争议

不同观点：
• **ummonk**：提到P320在枪套中意外击发的现象，尤其是即使正确套上枪套时也会发生。引用了具体视频展示该问题，质疑Sig的声明。
• **spl757**：区分了两种关于P320意外击发的指控，一种是手枪掉落时可能击发，另一种是枪在枪套中自行击发。对Sig的修复措施不信任，认为P320目前是不安全的武器，并表示不会再使用。
• **lenerdenator**：认为枪械制造商在大量生产新设计枪械时出现安全召回很正常，但批评Sig在处理P320问题时没有100%承担责任，尤其在获得重要军事合同后仍然否认问题，表示不会再购买Sig产品。
• **zxcvbn4038**：提到自己刚买了P320后就发现有关自发射的文章，虽然问题不常发生，但存在设计上的细微误差可能导致击发。提到一些执法机构正在悄悄用Glock 19替换P320，但自己仍保留P320，因为喜欢其大容量弹匣，同时已填写保修卡以防召回。
• **Khaine**：引用了Forgotten Weapons频道的视频讨论P320问题，提供额外信息来源。
• **mrbonner**：对比了P320和Glock，指出Glock没有外部安全杆，依赖双重扳机机制来防止意外击发，并质疑安全杆是否给人虚假的安全感。还提到大多数执法和军事机构使用Glock作为标准配置。
• **TheAmazingRace**：认为P320声誉差，但Sig的P365微型手枪表现出色，自己的P365经过大量射击无问题。
• **jleyank**：质疑携带时是否应上膛，建议在需要时再上膛以减少意外风险。

• **giantg2**：认为军用版P320的手动安全装置只是触发器阻块，没有额外保护作用，质疑军方对安全装置的要求是否合理。
• **colingauvin**：抱怨自己2018年购买的P320现在大幅贬值，对Sig的声明不满，认为产生了“斯特里斯效应”（欲盖弥彰的效果）。
• **nabla9**：认为军队广泛使用P320，因此其设计应着重考虑防呆设计，因为使用者中可能存在不谨慎的人。
• **darkteflon**：对枪械安全装置的作用提出疑问，询问是否携带时应关闭安全装置，或者是否误解了安全装置的目的。
• **sklargh**：提到P320问题可能导致的严重后果，特别是在美军核武器安保部队中也使用了该手枪，认为这是完全可以预防的悲剧。
• **nosignono**：表示自己和认识的人都多年不推荐使用P320，认为其危险，悲剧的发生是可预防的。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Sig P320手枪的意外击发问题，特别是枪在正确套上枪套时仍会击发，以及Sig在处理问题时的态度和修复措施是否足够。
• 对比了Glock和P320的安全机制，讨论了不同设计对防止意外击发的有效性。
• 提到P320问题对军方和执法机构的影响，以及对Sig产品声誉的打击。
• 对枪械安全装置的作用和设计提出了不同看法，反映了用户对枪械安全性的高度关注。
• 部分评论提到了P320贬值及其对消费者的经济影响，显示出对产品售后处理的不满。

NH News
Air Force unit suspends use of Sig Sauer pistol after shooting death of airman
New Hampshire Public Radio |
By
Todd Bookman
Published July 23, 2025 at 4:53 PM EDT
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Email
U.S. Air Force
A death on a Wyoming Air Force base involving a Sig Sauer-made pistol has led a unit of the Air Force to suspend use of the weapon pending further review.
A major division of the U.S. Air Force is immediately suspending use of a gun made by New Hampshire-based Sig Sauer, following a fatal shooting on a Wyoming base over the weekend.
The general in charge of the Air Force Global Strike Command, which comprises more than 33,000 personnel, said in a memo on Monday that he would be pausing the use of Sig Sauer’s M18 pistol immediately pending a “comprehensive review” of the weapon.
A spokesperson confirmed the pause on the weapon is directly related to the death on Sunday of an airman at F.E. Warren Airforce Base in Cheyenne, Wyoming. A statement on the base’s website
provided few details
about the fatality.
On Thursday, the base identified the airman as 21-year old Brayden Tyriq Lovan of Greenville, Kentucky who served in the 90th Security Forces Squadron. Lovan was a multi-sport athlete in high school who loved four-wheeling, hunting and video games, according to his obituary.
“We are deeply saddened by the loss of a valued member of our Mighty Ninety team,” said Col. Terry Holmes, a commander at the base. “Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with the Airman’s family, friends, and his fellow Defenders during this incredibly difficult time.”
A Pentagon spokesperson for the Air Force acknowledged the ongoing review of the M18 within the Global Strike Command, but didn’t say whether that investigation may expand to other units within the U.S. military that carry the pistol.
Get more New Hampshire news in your inbox: Sign up for our free Rundown newsletter.
"Weapons safety is a critical responsibility and we continue to prioritize the security of our Airmen and Guardians as they perform their challenging missions,” said the Air Force spokesperson.
Nearly all branches of the U.S. military have adopted the M18, as well as the M17, as their standard sidearms. The guns are modeled on Sig Sauer’s best-selling P320 pistol, which is sold on the civilian market and is widely used by law enforcement agencies around the country.
The death at the Wyoming base is the latest in a series of incidents in recent years that have raised questions about the safety of Sig’s marquee pistol. Both the P320 and the military’s version of the gun have faced repeated allegations of unintentional discharges, in which the gun allegedly fires without an intentional trigger pull. The gun has been at the center of dozens of civil lawsuits
claiming it has a design flaw
, though
judges
and juries have delivered
mixed verdicts
over the
company’s liability
in these shootings.
In March, Sig Sauer, whose headquarters are in Newington, announced it would take an aggressive approach to push back against allegations involving the P320, calling concerns about its safety “lies and misinformation.” That campaign included a successful effort this year to secure
a change in New Hampshire law
that will protect Sig Sauer from future liability lawsuits regarding allegations the gun should come equipped with certain safety features.
"Our hearts are with the service members and families impacted by the recent reported event at the F.E. Warren Air Force Base," a Sig Sauer spokesperson told NHPR. "We have offered assistance to the U.S. Military as they investigate the incident and remain willing to help in furtherance of their ongoing investigation."
We've been reporting on Sig Sauer for years. Read more here.
NH News
Jury awards $11M to man who says Sig Sauer P320 fired unintentionally
NH News
Documents detail U.S. soldiers shot by their own Sig Sauer guns; military says no reason for concern
NH News
22 more gun owners sue Sig Sauer alleging P320 fired unintentionally
NH News
The gun-maker SIG Sauer again receives state-backed bond to finance its expansion efforts in N.H.
NHPR has previously reported on unintentional discharges involving
the military’s version
of the weapon, including documented reports of serious injuries suffered by soldiers at U.S. military bases around the globe.
The U.S. Army, which selected the Sig Sauer pistol following a lengthy competitive bidding process, previously said that it had no concerns about the safety of the weapon and noted that it had undergone rigorous testing.
A spokesperson for the Global Strike Command said personnel will carry a different weapon while the investigation is underway, and that “all AFGSC bases will conduct 100% inspections of the M18 handguns to identify any immediate safety concerns.”
According to the unit’s website, the Air Force’s entire bomber fleet, as well as its nuclear command forces, operate under the Global Strike Command on bases stretching from Louisiana to Wyoming to Massac

data.title: New Aarch64 Back End
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文主要介绍了Zig编程语言主分支的最新更改，重点描述了2025年7月23日引入的新Aarch64后端。该后端由Jacob Young开发，包含多个相关文件，目前通过了79%的行为测试。与x86_64后端相比，Aarch64后端在代码生成速度上更快，二进制文件大小增加了约330KB。新后端采用了一些独特的架构设计，如在N个代码生成线程上进行指令编码，并拥有专属的双通道活性分析，简化了指令追踪机制。初步 benchmark 显示，Aarch64后端在多个性能指标上优于x86_64后端。另外，文中还提到2026年的Zig路线图计划，以及并行自托管代码生成的进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig编程语言的应用和其编译器相关技术细节的讨论

不同观点：
• conorbergin认为Zig正在成为他的一个多功能工具，尤其在GPU编程方面，可以通过编译成SPIR-V来实现相关功能。这表明Zig在多领域编程中的实用性和灵活性。

• ummonk对MIR的含义感到困惑，并提出疑问。他指出通常期望中间表示（IR）是平台无关的，但Zig中的MIR似乎更接近于Aarch64二进制，这暗示了对MIR具体实现细节的关注和对其平台依赖性的质疑。

• MuffinFlavored提问为何要避免使用LLVM后端，暗示了对Zig编译器技术选择背后的动机感兴趣，尤其是为何不采用已有的成熟技术如LLVM。

补充讨论：
• EricRiese的评论似乎是对一次代码变更的赞同，通过具体的数字（增加28,242行和删除3,737行）来表达对该变更的认可，但没有深入的技术讨论，更多是针对具体代码改动的支持表态。

• 争议焦点可能集中在Zig编译器的设计选择上，尤其是关于MIR的平台依赖性以及不使用LLVM后端的动机，这反映了对Zig技术路线的不同期待和理解。

July 23, 2025
New Aarch64 Backend
Author: Andrew Kelley & Jacob Young
Jacob
upstreamed his new backend yesterday
.
275 src/codegen/aarch64/Mir.zig
138 src/codegen/aarch64/abi.zig
11799 src/codegen/aarch64/encoding.zig
10981 src/codegen/aarch64/Select.zig
905 src/codegen/aarch64/Disassemble.zig
1653 src/codegen/aarch64/Assemble.zig
194 src/codegen/aarch64.zig
25945 total
Itâs passing 1547/1960 (79%) of the behavior tests compared to the LLVM backend.
Although it will grow in size as it approaches completion, it is considerably less logic than the x86 backend:
608 src/arch/x86_64/abi.zig
904 src/arch/x86_64/bits.zig
194471 src/arch/x86_64/CodeGen.zig
507 src/arch/x86_64/Disassembler.zig
980 src/arch/x86_64/Emit.zig
2790 src/arch/x86_64/encoder.zig
1072 src/arch/x86_64/Encoding.zig
2700 src/arch/x86_64/encodings.zon
689 src/arch/x86_64/Lower.zig
2152 src/arch/x86_64/Mir.zig
206873 total
In terms of binary size, it adds about 330KB (2%) to the compiler executable.
Jacob made some pretty neat architectural decisions with this one. For instance, it uses the actual machine code instruction encoding for the compilerâs internal MIR structure. This means that instruction encoding is done on the N codegen threads instead of the 1 linker thread.
All of the previous backends used a shared two-pass liveness analysis. This new backend has its own similar bespoke two-pass liveness analysis, except that the second pass also happens to generate all of the Mir in reverse at the same time! Besides cutting down on the number of passes that need to iterate over each function, making this backend speedier than other backends at generating code, this will allow backend-specific instruction lowerings that match multiple Air instructions to affect liveness and cause earlier instructions to become unused and end up not producing any code. This means that none of the incredibly complex deferred value tracking from the x86_64 backend is needed, allowing the tracking state machine to be vastly simplified.
Itâs not quite an apples-to-apples comparison due to missing features, but so far it is significantly faster than the x86 backend:

As for machine code quality, itâs too early to make reasonable comparisons, but suffice to say itâs looking quite promising! Weâll make another devlog entry when itâs capable of compiling more complex projects.
June 30, 2025
Zig Roadmap 2026
Author: Loris Cro
We scheduled a new Zig SHOWTIME episode for July 2nd to talk with Andrew about the Zig roadmap for 2026.
For more information check out
https://zig.show/episodes/41/
June 14, 2025
Parallel Self-Hosted Code Generation
Author: Matthew Lugg
Less than a week ago, we finally turned on the x86_64 backend by default for Debug builds on Linux and macOS. Today, weâve got a big performance improvement to it: weâve parallelized the compiler pipeline even more!
These benefits do not affect the LLVM backend, because it uses a lot more shared state; in fact, it is still limited to one thread, where every other backend was able to use two threads even before

• EricRiese的评论似乎是对一次代码变更的赞同，通过具体的数字（增加28,242行和删除3,737行）来表达对该变更的认可，但没有深入的技术讨论，更多是针对具体代码改动的支持表态。

• 争议焦点可能集中在Zig编译器的设计选择上，尤其是关于MIR的平台依赖性以及不使用LLVM后端的动机，这反映了对Zig技术路线的不同期待和理解。

主要讨论点：关于唐氏综合症相关科学进展的讨论及其伦理、社会影响

不同观点：
• **对唐氏综合症人群的个人经历和情感支持**：
  - [puppycodes] 分享了与唐氏综合症患者相处的个人经历，强调了这些人如何丰富了其生活，并带来了积极影响。
  - [juujian] 也提到自己认识的唐氏综合症患者如何让其生活更加丰富，提供了一种不同的世界观。

• **筛查与终止妊娠的讨论**：
  - [SJC_Hacker] 指出，在许多第一世界国家，通过孕期筛查和选择性终止妊娠，唐氏综合症的发生率已经在下降，特别是在道德上对堕胎限制较少的欧洲国家。文章链接提供了冰岛的例子，进一步说明了这一趋势。

• **科学方法与技术讨论**：
  - [daemonk] 提到了单倍型定相策略是关键方法，并提供了一篇相关论文链接，供有兴趣的人深入了解技术细节。

• **伦理与哲学反思**：
  - [vicnov] 提出，现代进步思想是否应将消除或治疗遗传性功能障碍视为“不道德”，这是一个值得研究的问题。
  - [issafram] 对研究的具体应用感到困惑，询问该技术是帮助现有唐氏综合症患者还是未来的怀孕。
  - [bjornnn] 进一步指出，该技术仅适用于体外受精，且可以通过选择其他精子捐献者来避免唐氏综合症，因此质疑此研究的实际应用价值。

• **技术应用的可能性与问题**：
  - [Scrounger] 提问，如果已经是成年人，是否可以通过该技术治疗唐氏综合症。
  - [moomoo11] 作为外行，对技术修改可能带来的副作用表示关注。

补充讨论：
• **资金来源与社会反应**：
  - [searine] 提到该研究由日本纳税人资助，指出了研究的资金背景。
  
• **幽默与创意想法**：
  - [dimensional_dan] 以幽默的方式提问，能否去除唐氏综合症的负面影响但保留其带来的快乐。
  - [iaaan] 提出了一个创意性的问题，是否可以通过增加一条染色体来平衡，而不是减去一条。

争议焦点：
• **伦理与社会价值问题**：部分讨论者如[vicnov]质疑通过技术手段消除唐氏综合症是否符合伦理，特别是在现代社会对“进步思想”的定义下。这与[SJC_Hacker]提到的通过终止妊娠减少唐氏综合症发生率的做法引发了一定的伦理争议。

• **技术应用的可行性与实际价值**：如[issafram]和[bjornnn]对该技术是否能真正帮助现有患者或未来怀孕的实际应用表示疑问，尤其在体外受精背景下，选择性捐献者方案可能更为直接有效。

data.title: Graphene OS: a security-enhanced Android build
data.author: madars
data.article_summary: GrapheneOS是一款专注于提升安全性和隐私保护的Android修改版，源自于2016年的CopperheadOS项目。在创始团队分裂后，Daniel Micay继续开发并推出了GrapheneOS，该项目由2023年成立的加拿大基金会支持，保持独立和开源。GrapheneOS基于Android开源项目，移除大量代码并增加多项安全改进，如强化内存分配库和控制流完整性功能。它主要支持Google Pixel 6到9设备，强调利用硬件内存标签功能增强安全性。安装过程提供网页和命令行两种方式，网页方式更为可靠。GrapheneOS旨在替代原生Android，提供更强的隐私保护，但安装新设备时需要手动调整一些设置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GrapheneOS的使用体验、功能评价、安全性与隐私保护、以及与Google Pixel设备支持相关的问题。

不同观点：
• **高度赞扬GrapheneOS**：一些用户（如jrexilius、bugsMarathon88）对GrapheneOS表示强烈赞赏，认为其安全性和隐私控制非常出色，给人一种发现“宝藏”的感觉。他们特别提到操作系统提供的细粒度控制、自动系统更新和无缝的电话功能。
• **对某些功能缺失或不足的担忧**：部分用户（如Sytten、b8）提到了一些实际使用中的问题，例如Google Pay无法使用、语音命令支持不足，以及对Google特有功能（如电话筛查和Hold for me）的依赖。
• **对设备支持数量有限的批评**：SchwKatze表示对GrapheneOS支持设备数量有限感到不满，尽管理解这是基于安全考虑，但希望能有低安全性版本以支持更多设备。
• **对安全功能的进一步需求**：throwaway-0001和其他用户建议增加密码胁迫功能，以在被迫给出密码时保护隐私。
• **对社区和信任的疑虑**：mjbale116对信任一个社区项目表示担忧，担心不良分子可能渗入并造成损害。相对的，h4kunamata则强烈支持GrapheneOS团队，认为其透明度和支持无与伦比，并驳斥了关于隐藏配置文件功能的误解。

补充讨论：
• **关于Pixel设备的支持问题**：minimalist提到了Google是否会继续发布设备树和驱动二进制文件的疑问，并讨论了这种做法对Pixel设备的市场需求影响。aussieguy1234则指出GrapheneOS缺乏对紧急服务定位支持的问题，这对某些户外活动爱好者来说是个重要安全隐患。
• **与其他ROM的比较**：z3c0和perching_aix讨论了GrapheneOS相较于其他ROM（如Lineage）的优势，特别是其对Google Play服务的支持，使得许多依赖Play服务的应用得以正常运行。
• **潜在用户的兴趣**：VladVladikoff表示GrapheneOS的特性甚至可能吸引Apple用户切换，并考虑尝试该系统。

争议焦点：
• **功能完整性与安全性之间的平衡**：一些用户希望增加更多功能（如Google特有功能和紧急服务支持），而另一些用户则认为GrapheneOS应优先考虑安全性和隐私保护，这种需求上的矛盾是讨论中的一个争议点。
• **对社区项目信任的问题**：部分用户对社区维护项目的安全性和可靠性表示担忧，而其他用户则坚定支持该项目的透明度和技术优势。

Graphene OS: a security-enhanced Android build
[LWN subscriber-only content]
By
Jonathan Corbet
July 24, 2025
People tend to put a lot of trust into their phones.  Those devices have
access to no end of sensitive data about our lives — our movements,
finances, communications, and more — so phones belonging to even relatively
low-profile people can be high-value targets.  Android devices run free
software, at least at some levels, so it should be possible to ensure that
they are working in their owners' interests.  Off-the-shelf Android
installations tend to fall short of that goal.  The
GrapheneOS
Android rebuild is an attempt
to improve on that situation.
GrapheneOS got its start as "CopperheadOS"; it was
reviewed here
in 2016.  A couple of years
later, though, an ugly dispute between the two founders of that project led
to its demise.  One of those founders, Daniel Micay, continued the work and
formed what eventually became GrapheneOS, which is, according to
this history page
, an
independent, open-source project that "
will never again be closely tied
to any particular sponsor or company
".  Work on GrapheneOS is supported
by a Canada-based foundation created in 2023; there appears to be almost no
public information available regarding this organization, though.
At its core, GrapheneOS is an effort to harden Android against a number of
threats and to make Android serve the privacy interests of its users.  It
is based on the
Android Open Source
Project
, but removes a lot of code and adds a long list of changes.
Some of those, such as a
hardened
malloc()
library
or the use of additional
control-flow-integrity features, will be mostly invisible to users (unless
they break apps, of course, which has evidently been known to happen).
Others are more apparent, but it is clear that a lot of effort has gone
into making the security improvements as unobtrusive as possible.
Like what you are reading?
Try LWN for free
for 1 month,
no credit card required.
Installation
Some Android rebuilds prioritize supporting a wide range of devices, often
with an eye toward keeping older devices working for as long as possible.
GrapheneOS is not one of those projects.  The
list of supported
hardware
is limited to Google Pixel 6 through Pixel 9
devices, with some trailing-edge support for Pixel 4 and 5
devices.  Even then, though, the newer devices are strongly recommended:
8th/9th generation Pixels provide a minimum guarantee of 7 years of
support from launch instead of the previous 5 year minimum
guarantee. 8th/9th generation Pixels also bring support for the
incredibly powerful hardware memory tagging security feature as
part of moving to new ARMv9 CPU cores. GrapheneOS uses hardware
memory tagging by default to protect the base OS and known
compatible user installed apps against exploitation, with the
option to use it for all apps and opt-out on a case-by-case basis
for the few incompatible with it.
My phone had been making it clear for a while that it could not be counted
on in the future, but the prospect of buying a new one inspired a lot of
trepidation.  Each new device seems to come with more privacy-hostile
"features" and intrusive AI "assistants"; finding all of the necessary
"disable" switches is a tedious and error-prone task.  That, along with the
news
that Google's "Gemini" feels increasingly entitled to a device-owner's data
regardless of its configuration, inspired the purchase of a Pixel 9
device that would be used to experiment with GrapheneOS to see if it could
replace stock Android for everyday use.
Flashing the firmware of an expensive device is always a bit of a nervous
prospect; the GrapheneOS installer is designed to minimize the amount of
fingernail biting involved in the process.  There are two installation
methods described in the documentation — a web-based install, and one that
works from the command line.  Naturally, I chose the command-line version.
The instructions
are
straightforward enough: download the installation image, connect the
device, and run the supplied script.  Said script ran to completion and
confidently declared victory at the end, but the device still only booted
into normal Android — a repeatable result, but not quite the intended one.
Some investigation turned up the (undocumented) fact that the web
installation method is seen as being rather more reliable than the
command-line version.  So I tried that, and it worked as intended; the
GrapheneOS experiment had begun in earnest.
First impressions
Stock Android includes some nice features to make the move to a new device
as easy as possible — unsurprising, given the strong incentive to get
people to make that move often.  Most of the data, apps, and configurations
that were on the old device will be automatically moved to the new one.
Graphene

data.title: Positron – A next-generation data science IDE
data.author: amai
data.article_summary: Positron 是 Posit PBC 推出的一款免费、下一代数据科学集成开发环境（IDE）。它是一个可扩展的多语言工具，支持编写代码和探索数据，并提供可重现的创作和发布环境。Positron 基于 Code OSS，用户可以参考 VS Code 文档了解基本功能。要开始使用 Positron，用户可以下载安装程序，查阅用户指南（如选择解释器和数据探索器），并通过 GitHub Discussions 提供反馈。Positron 采用 Elastic License 2.0 许可协议，其商标归 Posit Software, PBC 所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Positron IDE的优缺点及其开源性质的讨论

不同观点：
• ZeroCool2u：认为Positron IDE使用pyright和jedi而不是basedpyright，导致Python语言支持不佳。同时，对Positron声称是开源软件但有严格限制表示不满，提到之前因Posit的极端定价而不得不迁移到其他替代方案，且该过程非常麻烦。
• pks016：作为一名R和Python的日常用户，尝试过Posit但发现其不够稳定，包也不全。虽然对一些新功能如connections-pane感到兴奋，但切换需要时间。
• qsort：指出Positron缺乏好的SQL客户端，认为这是其相较于PyCharm或Visual Studio的劣势，强调需要强大的工具来完成复杂工作。
• williamstein：引用条款说明Positron并非完全开源，指出其对第三方提供的限制。
• alterom：认为Positron基于VSCode的开源代码，但未明确哪些功能或依赖不是开源或免费的，并指出捆绑GenAI助理可能是其盈利点。
• aleph_minus_one：提到Positron名称与一款超便携3D打印机重名，并提供了相关链接。
• mirkodrummer：对IDE领域被VSCode分支主导表示无奈。
• throwaway328：幽默地认为Emacs是唯一真正的下一代数据科学IDE。
• georgeg：期待一个支持Julia的多语言数据科学工具，对Positron不支持Julia表示失望。
• 7thaccount：认为Positron与Spyder IDE类似，具备代码编辑、变量检查和内嵌图表等功能，已满足需求。
• positron26：对网站被提前发布表示惊讶，但感谢带来的 adrenaline spike。
• greazy：作为Rstudio的重度用户，测试Positron发现其在Linux上缓慢且有bug，但正在改善。
• flusteredBias：简单表示喜欢使用Positron。
• iJohnDoe：提出一个具体项目问题，询问如何处理大型JSON文件的数据展示，表现出对数据科学工具的不熟悉。

data.author: chlobunnee
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：VRAM计算器的有效性、功能、以及对不同硬件的支持

不同观点：
• **支持特定计算器的观点**：
  - [zargon] 认为 https://apxml.com/tools/vram-calculator 更为全面，特别是因为它能够理解不同模型的注意力机制，并支持量化和微调。但也指出其局限性，如仅支持特定模型。
  
• **对计算器准确性持怀疑态度的观点**：
  - [kouteiheika] 指出训练内存的计算结果极不准确，尤其是在训练大模型时对FP32、BF16、梯度累积等方面的假设不准确。并以自身经验为例，说明实际需求远低于计算器估算。

• **对计算器实用性的批评**：
  - [funfunfunction] 认为该工具可能是GPU转销商的营销噱头。
  - [mdaniel] 批评计算器的用户界面和结果输出，认为其不实用。

• **对硬件支持的关注**：
  - [LorenDB], [jjmarr], [snvzz] 提到计算器缺乏对AMD GPU的支持。
  - [amanzi] 希望看到对RTX 5060 Ti的提及。
  - [timothyduong] 询问3090的支持情况。

补充讨论：
• **用户需求和功能改进建议**：
  - [chlobunnee] 分享了自己创建的计算器工具，旨在帮助研究人员选择合适的GPU，并寻求反馈以进一步改进功能，如增加GPU对比和部分GPU工作负载计算。
  
• **对特定模型支持的失望**：
  - [amelius] 提到选择LLama 3 70B模型后，所有GPU都不足以支持训练，显示出工具在处理大型模型时的局限性。

争议焦点：
• 计算器结果的准确性与实用性：部分用户认为计算器的结果过于夸大，不符合实际使用情况，尤其是在训练大模型时。这与工具设计者或支持者所宣称的全面性和准确性形成对比。
• 硬件支持的局限性：用户对计算器缺乏对AMD GPU等硬件的支持表示不满，反映了工具在兼容性上的不足。

data.title: Revisiting Moneyball
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary: 《Moneyball》讲述了2002年奥克兰运动家队在低预算下凭借数据分析（特别是上垒率OBP）取得成功的故事。球队总经理比利·比恩和统计学家保罗·德波德斯塔利用赛伯计量学挑战传统球探方法，通过客观数据如OBP做出球员选择，使决策更加透明和可量化。例如，他们以低价签下斯科特·哈特伯格，并通过让他改守一垒，充分发挥其上垒能力。运动家队在该年取得了103场胜利，并创下20场连胜的纪录，验证了数据分析策略的有效性。然而，随着运动家队离开奥克兰，该策略也被批评为导致低薪资预算，并被认为夸大了数据分析对比赛结果的影响。文章回顾了《Moneyball》的核心主题及其对体育界的持久影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Moneyball策略及其在体育和商业中的应用与影响

不同观点：
• **thom**：认为分析技术能帮助聪明的组织提升表现，但并不能保证成功。不够成熟的组织可能会因为确认偏误而失败，而中间群体的好工作常常被决策者忽视。

• **timshell**：Moneyball的核心教训不是单纯的分析，而是系统性地评估被低估的资产。在"后Moneyball时代"，传统球探方法重新受到重视，结合分析和传统方法才能获得市场优势。

• **cainxinth**：指出数据统计上季后赛表现不一定反映球队的真实水平，但球迷直觉上更看重季后赛表现，两者之间存在认知差异。

• **rsync**：通过巴西柔术的例子说明在比赛中坚持有效的策略是关键，但非分析派的球探更具人性化，可能在工作中获得更多乐趣。

• **johnnienaked**：运用博弈论的观点，指出如果只有一人使用Moneyball策略，它是一个竞争优势，但随着策略普及，这种优势会逐渐消失。

• **hhmc**：关注棒球比赛中本垒打、保送和三振增加的现象，质疑棒球规则是否需要改变以增加比赛的紧凑性和观赏性。

• **ryukoposting**：认为"Moneyball"这个名称引发了关于低薪支付球员的争议，但指出MLB近年来在缓解“三种真实结果”问题上做得不错，比如引入投球时钟。

• **alexpotato**：分享了自己在大学 paintball 中应用Moneyball策略的经验，强调分析技术不仅在于识别如上垒率等指标，更在于发现被低估的指标并应用它们。

• **hx8**：认为Moneyball的核心在于识别和展示被低估的资产在竞争环境中的价值，因在棒球中的应用而广泛传播。

• **xbar**：质疑谁误解了Moneyball的真正含义。

• **readthenotes1**：提出不超额支付明星球员而是雇佣能够完成工作的人是否是一种反劳工行为的问题。

补充讨论：
- Moneyball策略的应用与争议，包括对球员的低薪支付和市场效率问题。
- 传统方法与现代分析技术的结合，以及如何在不同领域中找到平衡点。
- 对棒球规则的潜在修改以改善比赛的节奏和观赏性。
- 分析技术在识别被低估指标中的实际应用与效果。

Revisiting Moneyball
Data, sports, payrolls, and memes
Pardis Noorzad
12 min read
·
13 hours ago

Listen

Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
Oakland Coliseum, September 2022.
Why are we
still
talking about Moneyball? Why am
I
talking about Moneyball?
For one, I’ve been meaning to write this post since 2019.
2018
even.
Zoom image will be displayed
My friends are the best. From
here
.
The
book
was published in 2003, and the
movie
was released in 2011. It feels silly to rehash, except the whole thing fascinates fans two decades later. Why? On the one hand, it is loved because it tells the classic underdog story while suggesting that nerdy analytics contributed to the wins; on the other, and especially as the A’s leave Oakland, it is blamed for encouraging low payrolls and critiqued for overstating the impact of analytics on the 2002 season and beyond.
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
From
here
,
here
, and
here
.
In this post, I’ll go over
the author
’s intentions for writing the book, followed by popular critiques of Moneyball. The goal is to address some of the recurring debates as we cover the main themes and provide historical context for each.
Understanding Moneyball
Let’s begin by discussing the book’s central themes and what the author found intriguing about the A’s in 2002. Moneyball has been so influential that many of these themes have since become memes.
Analytics leads to more transparent decision-making.
The A’s GM, Billy Beane, working with statistician Paul DePodesta, used sabermetrics to challenge traditional scouting methods that relied on more subjective evaluations.
This transparency allowed decisions regarding players to be justified through objective metrics. When the A’s signed Scott Hatteberg or traded for David Justice, they could point to specific evidence, like on-base percentage (OBP) or plate discipline, to justify their decision. This approach also aimed to make decision makers accountable for outcomes by establishing a decision-making framework that could be communicated, replicated, and thus improved upon.
Getting on base is undervalued, and teams can use this to their advantage.
While scouts focused on batting average, home runs, and RBIs, Beane recognized that OBP had a stronger correlation with run production than any of the traditional metrics. [1][2]
Zoom image will be displayed
The math was simple: teams that get on base more frequently score more runs, and teams that score more runs win more games. Yet in 2002, players with high OBP were available at below-market prices. Players like Scott Hatteberg (.374 OBP in 2002) and David Justice (.370 OBP) were affordable because their most valuable skill, i.e., getting on base, wasn’t appreciated sufficiently by the market.
The strategy worked: the 2002 A’s ranked 2nd in the American League (AL) in OBP (.339) despite having the third-lowest payroll in baseball.
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
In 2002, the A’s achieved 4th highest OBP (.349) with 3rd lowest payroll ($40M) [3][4].
Scott Hatteberg is undervalued.
Scott Hatteberg was available at a below-market price due to perceived limitations. The former Boston Red Sox catcher developed nerve damage in his throwing elbow, making catching nearly impossible and leaving him without a clear defensive position.
Oakland signed Hatteberg to first base for $950K on a one-year contract after Colorado declined salary arbitration. The A’s saw past the injury to identify his core value: exceptional plate discipline and on-base skills. His .367 OBP in 2000 and .410 OBP in 1999 demonstrated an ability to get on base that strongly correlated with offensive production.
The position switch to first base was unprecedented; he had never played the position professionally. He learned first base during spring training with infield coach Ron Washington.
Hatteberg’s 2002 performance validated the analytical approach: .280/.374/.433 slash line, 68 walks versus 56 strikeouts, and 4.15 pitches per plate appearance (3rd in AL). His defining moment came on September 4, 2002, when his walk-off home run against Kansas City secured the A’s 20th consecutive victory and set an AL record.
Hatteberg hit a walk-off home run to give the A’s a 12–11 win and a then-AL record 20-game winning streak.
The streak is historic and remarkable.
The 20-game winning streak (August 13 — September 4, 2002) became the dramatic centerpiece of the Moneyball story.
The streak’s climactic finish, Oakland blowing an 11–0 lead to Kansas City before Hatteberg’s walk-off home run, provided Hollywood-worthy drama that helped make the analytical approach culturally compelling.
More importantly, the streak occurred during a season where the A’s won 103 games despite having one of baseball’s lowest payrolls.
Zoom image will be displayed
Zoom image will be displayed
The A’s achieved 103 wins (tied for MLB lead) with the 3rd lowest payroll

data.author: bilekas
data.article_summary: 文章简要总结了全球支付处理市场的双寡头垄断现象，主要由Visa和Mastercard主导。这两家公司控制了中国以外约90%的支付处理市场，合并市值达约8500亿美元。它们的成功源于20世纪50年代信用卡行业的兴起，Diners Club和American Express早期开拓了这一领域。随后，Visa和Mastercard从美国的主要银行中脱胎而出，通过先行者优势和限制性合同巩固了市场地位。其业务模式类似于铁路系统，依赖网络效应和规模化运营，拥有高运营利润。然而，近年来它们面临挑战，如亚马逊谈判降低手续费，以及印度RuPay等国家支付处理机构的崛起，威胁其主导地位。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：各国支付系统和美国支付卡网络的竞争，尤其是美国对巴西Pix和印度UPI等公共支付基础设施崛起的反应，以及支付系统中的费用、监管和垄断问题。

不同观点：
• **支持公共支付基础设施**：[mzitelli]和[zaptheimpaler]认为，像巴西的Pix和印度的UPI这样的公共支付基础设施提供了免费且即时的交易，对社会非常有利。他们指出，这些系统削弱了Visa和MasterCard等私人支付网络的垄断地位，节省了大量交易费用，并提高了支付效率。[zaptheimpaler]特别提到，让私营公司控制关键国家基础设施是不可理喻的。

• **美国保护现状**：[mzitelli]提到，美国政府对Pix展开调查，表明其方向是保护现有的支付体系，避免受到新兴公共基础设施的冲击。这暗示了美国政府可能在试图保护Visa和MasterCard等传统支付网络的利益。

• **欧盟的有效监管**：[pavlov]强调，欧盟对信用卡手续费设置了上限，成功控制了交易费用，相较于美国2%的费用，欧盟的0.2%-0.3%显得更加合理。这显示了监管在控制垄断企业方面的有效性。

• **中国的自主发展**：[topdan]提到，中国通过避免开放金融服务市场，成功发展了自己的支付系统，避免了Visa和MasterCard的垄断。尽管美国曾起诉中国并胜诉，但中国依然建立了自己的支付体系。

• **商家的实际需求**：[rprend]指出，尽管商家声称关心支付手续费，但在实际操作中，他们更关心销售转化率。因此，新的支付系统如果想要获得支持，必须能够带来新的收入，而不仅仅是降低现有成本。

• **欺诈和支付系统安全**：[rprend]和[MinimalAction]提到，现有的ACH系统存在欺诈风险，而像UPI和Pix这样的系统在遇到诈骗时难以追回资金。此外，美国的支付系统依赖于ACH和可能的未来技术如FedNow，这带来了一些技术和安全挑战。

• **对私营支付系统的不满**：[h4kunamata]、[everyone]等对Visa和MasterCard的垄断表示不满，特别提到它们在内容审查和支付处理方面的权力过大，甚至影响了像Steam和Itch.io这样的平台对成人内容的限制。这种自我审查被视为不民主和不道德的。

补充讨论：
• **国际支付体系的去美元化趋势**：[h4kunamata]提到，越来越多的国家开始在国际贸易中使用本国货币而非美元，这表明全球支付体系可能正在经历“去美元化”的趋势。

• **历史和文化视角**：[frankfrank13]通过文化作品中的引用，幽默地评论了Diners信用卡的命运，暗示了一些支付系统在历史中的演变和挣扎。

• **俄罗斯的Mir支付系统**：[DmitryO]提到俄罗斯的Mir支付系统已经在约10个国家开始使用，显示出在某些地区非西方支付系统的扩展潜力。

争议焦点：
• 美国政府是否在保护Visa和MasterCard等传统支付网络的利益，阻碍像Pix这样的公共支付基础设施的全球扩展。
• 私营支付系统如Visa和MasterCard在内容审查和支付处理方面的权力是否过大，是否应该受到更严格的政府监管。

Visa and Mastercard: The Global Payment Duopoly
Visa and Mastercard: The Global Payment Duopoly
1
minutes reading time
Published
1 Mar 2024
Author:
Peter Westberg
Reviewed by:
Kasper Karlsson
Updated
26 May 2025
The global payments processing market is dominated by two major players: Visa and Mastercard. These two companies account for 90% of all payment processing outside of China and have a combined market value of approximately $850 billion. How is it possible that, in the era of global competition, such a large market niche is completely dominated by only two players? Let's explore this in-depth and examine the increasing challenges they face in protecting their market positions.
Key Insights
Dominant market share:
Visa and Mastercard control approximately 90% of all payment processing outside of China, showcasing a significant duopoly in the global payments processing market with a combined market value of around $850 billion.
Historical foundations:
The origins of the credit card industry trace back to the 1950s with companies like Diners Club and American Express pioneering the space. Visa and Mastercard emerged from major American banks, leveraging first-mover advantages and restrictive contracts to solidify their market position.
Competitive advantages:
The analogy of payment processing to railroads highlights their control over digital transactions, benefiting from network effects, scalability, and distribution through major banks.
Challenges to the duopoly:
Recent years have seen challenges to their dominance, from major companies like Amazon negotiating for lower fees, to the rise of national payment processors like RuPay in India.
Historical Context: Origins of the Credit Card
In 1950, Diners Club issued the first modern credit card to exist, representing the type of cards familiar to us today. Seeing its success, a range of large financial institutions and other companies in America began issuing their own form of credit cards.
In 1958,
American Express
emerged as one of the first major players to issue its own charge cards. Public interest was so substantial that American Express had already issued 250,000 of its cards before the official launch date, despite the card's high annual fee of $6 at the time ($64 inflation-adjusted).
Bank of America
entered the credit card arena in the same year, introducing a product that was initially exclusive to California. In 1966, Bank of America's card began to be licensed for use in other states, and the name of this business was changed to
Visa
. It was spun off as an independent corporation in 1976.
The same year that Bank of America launched Visa, in 1966, a consortium of competitors established the Interbank Card Association (ICA), which would ultimately introduce Master Charge shortly after, which saw a name change to
Mastercard
in 1979. Today, Mastercard and Visa are the two biggest credit card networks globally, controlling roughly 90% of the payment processing market outside of China. Due to their duopoly and scalable underlying business models, Visa and Mastercard boast the highest operating margins among all companies in the S&P 500, with 67% and 57% respectively in 2023.
How Visa and Mastercard Came to Dominate
Since debit and credit cards originated in America, Visa and MasterCard had a head start from a global perspective, both being founded in 1966. However, as previously mentioned, Diners Club issued its first credit card in 1950, followed by American Express, which pivoted to credit cards in 1958. American Express issued the first plastic credit card in 1959, and the magnetic stripes were developed by
IBM
.
This radical shift by American Express, which originated as a transportation and currency exchange company in 1850, was a response to the changing needs of post-war America. During this era, consumerism was on the rise, and a growing middle class with an increasing disposable income. The American Express card, initially a paper card with an annual fee, allowed cardholders to make purchases on credit and settle their bills at the end of each month.
The American Express Card revolutionized the payment landscape, fostering a shift from cash and checks to electronic payments. Consequently, American Express can be considered the true pioneer and first-mover in the credit card and payment processing space. Despite this, Visa and Mastercard would subsequently come to dominate almost the entire market.
In response to the success of American Express, Visa and Mastercard were born out of the major banks in America, arguably the most crucial variable in the creation of this global duopoly. For a long time, Mastercard and Visa used restrictive contracts to their advantage. Merchants were therefore left with no choice but to deal with these companies due to the lack of viable alternatives. data.title: RE#: High performance derivative-based regular expression matching (2024)
data.author: fanf2
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为RE#的正则表达式匹配工具及其理论基础。RE#基于符号衍生，不使用回溯，支持补集、交集和前后查找等操作。理论分析和实验表明，其主要匹配算法具有线性时间复杂度。在多项基准测试中，RE#比最快的Rust正则引擎快71%以上，并在扩展基准测试中大幅超越其他引擎， often by several orders of magnitude。该工具在形式语言与自动机理论领域具有重要意义。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：正则表达式匹配语义、布尔操作符的支持及其语义、正则表达式引擎的工业实现历史

不同观点：
• kazinator认为RE#支持的匹配语义是左侧最长匹配（POSIX），而不是左侧贪婪匹配（PCRE）语义。对于如何在回溯引擎中支持扩展的布尔操作符以及其预期语义存在疑问。具体来说，| 操作符在回溯语义中是非交换的，导致一些关键的分配律不再保持匹配语义。例如，A|B|C|D 在回溯引擎中会从左到右依次尝试匹配，如果A匹配成功，则不再尝试B、C、D。kazinator进一步举例说明，在处理"c.r|carp.t"和输入"carpet-odor"时，贪婪匹配会选择较短的匹配"car"，而最长匹配语义则会选择更长的匹配"carpet"。

• 针对上述问题，kazinator指出最长匹配语义符合集合论解释，其中|操作符是可交换的，R1|R2等同于R2|R1，代表R1和R2匹配的字符串的并集。

• 关于正则表达式工业实现的历史，kazinator指出第一个在命令式语言（C#）中使用导数实现标准正则表达式的工业实现是在2019年，但其在2010年已经在TXR中实现了该功能，并提供了具体的提交哈希和日期作为证据。

• omgtehlion提到RE#的源代码库似乎已被删除，并询问是否有人有实际代码的链接。随后自己回答，指出该功能似乎已经部分合并到dotnet本身，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于回溯引擎中|操作符的非交换性及其对匹配结果的影响。kazinator认为这种行为是不合理的，并提倡最长匹配语义。
• 正则表达式匹配语义的具体实现及其对实际应用的影响是另一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 关于正则表达式引擎工业实现的历史，kazinator提供了早期的实现证据，指出了其贡献，并纠正了相关时间线。

Title:
RE#: High Performance Derivative-Based Regex Matching with Intersection, Complement and Lookarounds
Authors:
Ian Erik Varatalu
,
Margus Veanes
,
Juhan-Peep Ernits
View a PDF of the paper titled RE#: High Performance Derivative-Based Regex Matching with Intersection, Complement and Lookarounds, by Ian Erik Varatalu and Margus Veanes and Juhan-Peep Ernits
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present a tool and theory RE# for regular expression matching that is built on symbolic derivatives, does not use backtracking, and, in addition to the classical operators, also supports complement, intersection and lookarounds. We develop the theory formally and show that the main matching algorithm has input-linear complexity both in theory as well as experimentally. We apply thorough evaluation on popular benchmarks that show that RE# is over 71% faster than the next fastest regex engine in Rust on the baseline, and outperforms all state-of-the-art engines on extensions of the benchmarks often by several orders of magnitude.

• omgtehlion提到RE#的源代码库似乎已被删除，并询问是否有人有实际代码的链接。随后自己回答，指出该功能似乎已经部分合并到dotnet本身，并提供了一个GitHub链接作为参考。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于回溯引擎中|操作符的非交换性及其对匹配结果的影响。kazinator认为这种行为是不合理的，并提倡最长匹配语义。

这篇文章介绍了一种鲜为人知的编程范式——连接式编程（concatenative programming）。作者试图通过撰写教程来推广这一概念，类似于John Hughes的经典文章《Why Functional Programming Matters》。文章首先指出人们对“连接式编程”定义存在分歧，甚至有人认为这一术语没有实际意义。然而，作者认为连接式编程的核心在于使用函数组合而非函数应用，这与应用式编程语言（applicative language）不同。

文章接着解释了连接式编程的基本原理，强调其通过隐式组合函数来简化编程，避免了命名状态和变量处理等问题。相比传统的函数式编程，连接式编程更简单且更“函数式”。作者还通过示例展示了连接式编程的表达方式，如使用后缀表示法来执行操作。文章最后承诺会进一步讲解连接式编程的工作原理、类型系统及其优缺点。

Introduction
There doesn’t
seem to be a good tutorial out there for concatenative programming, so I
figured I’d write one, inspired by the classic “Why Functional
Programming Matters” by John Hughes. With any luck it will get more people interested in the topic, and give me a URL to hand people when they ask what the heck I’m so excited about.
Foremost, there seems to be some disagreement over what the term “concatenative” actually means.
This Stack Overflow answer
by Norman Ramsey even goes so far as to say:
“…it
is not useful to use the word ‘concatenative’ to describe programming
languages. This area appears to be a private playground for
Manfred von Thun
.
There is no real definition of what constitutes a concatenative
language, and there is no mature theory underlying the idea of a
concatenative language.”
This is rather harsh, and,
well, wrong. Not entirely wrong, mind, just rather wrong. But it’s not
surprising that this kind of misinformation gets around, because
concatenative programming isn’t all that well known. (I aim to change
that.)
Concatenative programming is so called because
it uses function
composition
instead of function
application
—a non-concatenative language is thus called
applicative
.
That’s the defining difference, and it’s as “real” a definition as I
need, because, well, it’s the one that people are using. Bang.
Descriptivism.
One of the problems with functional
programming is that the oft-touted advantages—immutability, referential
transparency, mathematical purity, &c.—don’t
immediately
seem
to apply in the real world. The reason “Why Functional Programming
Matters” was necessary in the first place was that functional
programming had been mischaracterised as a paradigm of negatives—no
mutation, no side-effects—so everybody knew what you
couldn’t
do, but few people grasped what you
could
.
There is a similar problem with concatenative programming. Just look at the Wikipedia introduction:
A
concatenative programming language is a point-free programming language
in which all expressions denote functions and the juxtaposition of
expressions denotes function composition. The combination of a
compositional semantics with a syntax that mirrors such a semantics
makes concatenative languages highly amenable to algebraic manipulation.
This is all true—and all irrelevant to your immediate problem of
why you should care
. So in the next sections, I will show you:
How concatenative programming works
How typing in a concatenative language works
How concatenative languages are efficient
What concatenative languages are
not
good for
Where to go for more information
Now let’s get started!
♦ ♦ ♦
The Basics
In
an applicative language, functions are applied to values to get other
values. λ-calculus, the basis of functional languages, formalises
application as “β-reduction”, which just says that if you have a
function (
f
x
=
x
+ 1) then you can substitute a call to that function (
f
y
) with its result (
y
+ 1). In λ-calculus, simple juxtaposition (
f
x
) denotes application, but function composition must be handled with an explicit composition function:
compose := λ
f
. λ
g
. λ
x
.
f
(
g
x
)
This definition says “the composition (compose) of two functions (
f
and
g
) is the result of applying one (
f
) to the result of the other (
g
x
)”,
which is pretty much a literal definition. Note that this function can
only be used to compose functions of a single argument—more on this
later.
In concatenative languages, composition is implicit
: “
f
g
” is the composition of
f
and
g
. However, this does not mean that function application becomes explicit—it actually becomes
unnecessary
. And as it turns out, this peculiar fact makes these languages a whole lot simpler to build, use, and reason about.
The
untyped λ-calculus is a relatively simple system. However, it and the
many systems derived from it still need three kinds of term—variables,
lambdas, and applications—as well as a number of rules about how to
correctly replace variable names when applying functions. You have to
deal with name binding, closures, and scope. For a supposedly low-level
language, it has quite a bit of inherent complexity.
Concatenative languages have a much simpler basis—
there are
only
functions and compositions
, and evaluation is just the
simplification
of functions. It is never necessary to deal with named state—there are
no variables. In a sense, concatenative languages are “more functional”
than traditional functional languages! And yet, as we will see, they are
also easy to implement efficiently.
♦ ♦ ♦
Composition
Let’s say we want to multiply a couple of numbers. In a typical concatenative language, this looks like:
2 3 ×
There are two weird things about this.
First,
we use postfix notation (2 3 ×) rather than the prefix notation (× 2 3)
that is common in the functional world, or the infix notation (2 × 3)
that most languages provide for convenience. There is nothing

a concatenative language from having infix op

data.title: Superfunctions: A universal solution against sync/async fragmentation in Python
data.author: pomponchik
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Python中同步和异步代码分裂的问题，以及一个名为`transfunctions`的库如何通过模板和代码生成来解决这一问题。Python使用`async`和`await`关键字来实现异步编程，导致代码被“染色”，同步和异步函数不能直接互调，导致代码重复。`transfunctions`库通过将一个函数模板转换为普通函数、异步函数或生成器函数，从而避免代码重复。该库基于AST（抽象语法树）进行代码生成，允许开发者创建“超级函数”，这些函数可以根据使用方式表现为普通函数、异步函数或生成器函数。这样，开发者无需手动区分函数的同步或异步特性，从而简化代码编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中的同步与异步编程模型及其复杂性

不同观点：
• **nilslindemann**：认为当前的异步（async）命名不准确，建议重新定义命名和操作符。他提议一种新的编程方式，通过单个操作符来指定代码的执行顺序，允许并行或异步执行，但在某个点必须汇合（join）以继续执行。他强调当前的命名导致了不必要的复杂性。

• **PaulHoule**：对nilslindemann的提议持怀疑态度，认为其方案会导致编写和使用超级函数（superfunctions）都很 awkward。他提出，异步编程通常需要访问网络、管道或进行睡眠操作，建议将这些上下文封装在对象中，并通过类来实现。他还提到，可以通过包装HTTP API来减少重复代码。

• **operator-name**：认为nilslindemann的方案可能会引入更多功能变体，增加复杂性。他提到asgiref和synchronicity作为现有解决方案，分别通过简单的包装器和100%异步代码暴露同步和异步接口来解决此问题。他担心nilslindemann的方案可能会导致性能问题和理解困难。

• **pomponchik**：支持超级函数的概念，认为它可以减少Python生态系统中同步和异步版本的代码重复，提供客户端选择的机会，类似于Zig语言的实现。

• **RS-232**：认为nilslindemann的方案仍然在模板函数中复制代码，建议装饰器应自动抽象出上下文管理器。他提出I/O绑定操作可以是异步的，而其他操作应该是同步的。

• **rsyring**：对使用波浪号（~）调用函数的语法和机制提出质疑，指出其限制（如无法使用返回值和异常处理）。他认为自己不是该库的目标用户。

• **OutOfHere**：建议放弃Python中的异步编程，因为Python的未来是自由线程的，而异步是单线程的。他认为即使现在不需要多线程，将来也会需要，使用自由线程可以避免完全重写代码。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效地实现和使用同步与异步编程模型，减少复杂性和代码重复。
• 不同的解决方案包括重新定义命名和操作符、封装对象、使用现有工具如asgiref和synchronicity、以及抽象出超级函数。
• 对异步编程的实用性和未来发展方向存在不同看法，部分人认为异步模型过于复杂且受限，而另一些人则支持通过现有工具和模式来简化问题。

This library is designed to solve one of the most important problems in python programming - dividing all written code into 2 camps: sync and async. We get rid of code duplication by using templates.
Table of contents
Quick start
The problem
Code generation
Markers
Superfunctions
Quick start
Install it:
pip install transfunctions
And use:
from
asyncio
import
run

transfunctions
import

transfunction

,
async_context
,
generator_context

transfunction

print

'so, '

''
)

sync_context
:
print
(
"it's just usual function!"
)
with
async_context
:
print
(
"it's an async function!"
)
with
generator_context
:
print
(
"it's a generator function!"
)
yield
function
=
template
.
get_usual_function
()
function
()
#> so, it's just usual function!
async_function
=
template
.

()

(

())
#> so, it's an async function!
generator_function
=
template
.
get_generator_function
()
list

generator_function
())
#> so, it's a generator function!
As you can see, in this case, 3 different functions were created based on the template, including both common parts and unique ones for a specific type of function.
You can also quickly try out this and other packages without having to install using
instld
.
The problem
Since the
asyncio
module appeared in Python more than 10 years ago, many well-known libraries have received their asynchronous alternates. A lot of the code in the Python ecosystem has been
duplicated
, and you probably know many such examples.
The reason for this problem is that the Python community has chosen a way to implement asynchrony expressed through syntax. There are new keywords in the language, such as
async
and
await
. Their use makes the code so-called "
multicolored
": all the functions in it can be red or blue, and depending on the color, the rules for calling them are different. You can only call blue functions from red ones, but not vice versa.
I must say that implementing asynchronous calls using a special syntax is not the only solution. There are languages like Go where runtime can independently determine "under the hood" where a function should be asynchronous and where not, and choose the correct way to call it. A programmer does not need to manually "colorize" their functions there. Personally, I think that choosing a different path is the mistake of the Python community, but that's not what we're discussing here.
The solution offered by this library is based on templating. You can take a certain function as a template and generate several others based on it: regular, asynchronous, or generator. This allows you to avoid duplicating code where it was previously impossible. And all this without major changes in Python syntax or in the internal structure of the interpreter. We're just "sweeping under the carpet" syntax differences. Combined with the idea of context-aware functions, this makes for an even more powerful tool:
superfunctions
. This allows you to create a single function object that can be handled as you like: as a regular function, as an asynchronous function, or as a generator. The function will behave the way you use it. Thus, this library solves the problem of code duplication caused by the syntactic approach to marking asynchronous execution sections.

generating code
at the
AST
level.

template

(
'something'
)

produce
functions:
print
(
template
)

get_usual_function
method from it:
function
=
template
.
get_usual_function
()
function
()
#> something

from
asyncio
import
run
async_function
=
template
.
get_async_function
()
run
(
async_function
())
#> something

• **rsyring**：对使用波浪号（~）调用函数的语法和机制提出质疑，指出其限制（如无法使用返回值和异常处理）。他认为自己不是该库的目标用户。

• **OutOfHere**：建议放弃Python中的异步编程，因为Python的未来是自由线程的，而异步是单线程的。他认为即使现在不需要多线程，将来也会需要，使用自由线程可以避免完全重写代码。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效地实现和使用同步与异步编程模型，减少复杂性和代码重复。
• 不同的解决方案包括重新定义命名和操作符、封装对象、使用现有工具如asgiref和synchronicity、以及抽象出超级函数。
• 对异步编程的实用性和未来发展方向存在不同看法，部分人认为异步模型过于复杂且受限，而另一些人则支持通过现有工具和模式来简化问题。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 的 MCP（Microsoft Copilot Plugins）支持情况及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [jngiam1] 认为 OpenAI 的 MCP 支持令人困惑。作为终端用户，只能在深度研究模式下使用 `search` 和 `fetch` 工具，而开发者通过 API 可以使用完整的 MCP 工具集。此外，Custom GPTs 支持任意操作但不支持 MCP，并且仅支持 4o 和 4.1 模型，这限制了 o-系列模型的使用。总体感觉理解何时能用什么功能比实际需要的要复杂。

• [ascorbic] 质疑是否有任何变化，认为当前状态已经维持了几个月，MCP 仅限于专业版和企业版，且只能在深度研究模式下使用。

• [cube2222] 指出支持非常奇怪，目前的 MCP 支持似乎只针对包含 `search` 和 `fetch` 两个工具的自定义高层次协议，而非所有可用的 MCP 服务器，因此并不是全面的 MCP 支持。

• [maxwellg] 对 MCP 支持感到满意，认为相比基于 OpenAPI 的 Custom Actions 或 Custom GPTs，MCP 服务器能够更好地将工具定义部分移到服务器端，从而在版本控制、功能标记等方面有更好的控制。

• [babyshake] 提出 MCP 是否已经战胜 A2A（API to API）模式的问题，询问这是否是对当前形势的误解。

• [kinduff] 赞赏 OpenAI 将 MCP 支持整合到现有工具中的做法，认为这是非常聪明的策略。

• [DiabloD3] 对 OpenAI 没有解释为何要使用其 MCP API 表示不满，并提出 AI 行业的各种问题，如客户数据的不当处理、导致客户数据或财务损失的操作等，认为提供 MCP 服务可能导致 GDPR 或其他数据泄露事件，最终让使用者承担风险，而 OpenAI 自己则为了盈利而忽视这些问题。

• [ipsum2] 指出标题具有一定误导性，因为 MCP 支持仅适用于 API，而不适用于网页/移动端界面。

补充讨论：
• MCP 与 A2A 模式的对比及哪个更具优势是另一个讨论点，[babyshake] 提出了 MCP 是否已经胜出的问题。
• 安全与隐私问题，尤其是 GDPR 合规性，是 [DiabloD3] 关注的焦点，认为 OpenAI 没有充分说明使用 MCP 服务可能带来的法律风险。
• 用户体验和支持范围的局限性也被多次提及，尤其是 MCP 工具的限制和使用场景的模糊性导致了用户的困惑。

data.title: The Secret Life of Fsync (2023)
data.author: RGBCube
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 fsync 函数及其在数据持久性和性能方面的表现进行的技术讨论。

不同观点：
• 一些开发者认为 fsync 对于确保数据持久性至关重要，特别是在数据库或文件系统的应用中。他们指出，虽然 fsync 可能导致性能下降，但为了数据完整性，这是必要的代价。例子包括数据库事务的持久性保证。

• 另一部分开发者则关注 fsync 对性能的负面影响，特别是在高吞吐量或低延迟需求的系统中。他们建议尽量减少 fsync 的使用，或者通过缓存和批量写入等技术来优化性能。有人提到，在某些实时系统中，fsync 的延迟可能导致不可接受的性能瓶颈。

• 还有观点认为，操作系统或文件系统层面的优化可以减轻 fsync 带来的性能问题。他们建议改进底层实现，比如通过更好的 I/O 调度或异步操作来提高效率。有评论提到了不同操作系统对 fsync 实现的差异，并指出 Linux 的 fsync 性能问题较多。

• 一部分评论集中讨论了 fsync 使用的复杂性，特别是在多线程或分布式系统中的应用。他们指出，fsync 的行为可能会导致竞态条件或数据不一致的问题，需要谨慎处理。例子包括多线程程序中如何正确同步以避免数据竞争。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还涉及了 fsync 与现代存储设备（如 SSD）的兼容性问题。有人认为 SSD 的出现使得 fsync 的作用有所减弱，因为 SSD 本身具有更好的写入性能和内部缓存管理。

• 争议的焦点之一是，在实际应用中如何平衡数据完整性和性能需求。部分开发者认为可以通过应用层面的设计来避免频繁的 fsync 调用，而其他人则坚持认为 fsync 是不可或缺的工具。

• 链接中的讨论也提到了实际项目中的经验，比如在 PostgreSQL 或 LevelDB 等数据库系统中如何有效地使用 fsync。这些经验分享提供了实际应用中的论据和例子，进一步丰富了讨论。

data.title: Show HN: Easy Python Time Parsing
data.author: felixnext
data.article_summary:
"Python Time Helper" 是一个轻量级 Python 库，用于简化日期时间处理，支持时区操作。主要特性包括：

1. **万能日期时间解析**：自动解析多种日期时间格式和时间戳。
2. **时区操作**：支持通过名称或缩写处理时区，如 IST、PST，并可轻松转换时区。
3. **日期时间操作**：包括时间舍入（按小时、天、周等）和时间差计算。
4. **可选依赖**：支持与 Pandas、NumPy 集成，便于处理 DataFrame 和数组。

安装方式：
- 基础功能：`pip install time-helper`
- 支持 Pandas：`pip install time-helper[pandas]`
- 支持 NumPy：`pip install time-helper[numpy]`

示例：
```python
from time_helper import any_to_datetime, make_aware, round_time

dt = any_to_datetime("2024-03-15 10:30:45")
aware_dt = make_aware("2024-03-15")
rounded = round_time(dt, "H")
```

该库适用于需要灵活处理日期时间的项目，提供简单直观的 API。

不同观点：
• 支持添加 `strptime()`：
  - `watersb` 引用了GitHub上的一个issue（https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/41431），指出Python 3.14 新增的 `strptime()` 构造函数相当于 `datetime(*(time.strptime(date_string, format)[0:6]))`。这意味着开发者可以通过 `strptime()` 更方便地将日期字符串解析为日期对象。
  - 支持者可能认为这种改动简化了时间处理的代码，使代码更加简洁易读，减少了手动解析的需求。

• 反对或质疑添加 `strptime()`：
  - 一些开发者可能会质疑这种改动的必要性，认为现有的 `datetime.strptime()` 已经能够满足解析日期字符串的需求。新增的构造函数可能导致冗余，增加学习成本。
  - 另一个潜在的反对理由是，这种改动可能会导致向后兼容性问题，尤其是对于那些已经使用了类似方法解析时间的项目，可能会产生冲突或混淆。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现细节：
  - `strptime()` 的实现细节被提及，指出其功能是通过解析日期字符串并返回前六个元素（年、月、日、小时、分钟、秒），然后传递给 `datetime` 构造函数。
  - 开发者可能会进一步讨论该实现的性能问题，尤其是与现有方法相比，是否会引入额外的开销或潜在的bug。

• 社区反馈和未来发展：

  - 还有人可能会提到，这种改动是否符合Python语言的发展方向，即简化常见任务的实现，同时保持代码的可读性和简洁性。

争议的焦点：
• 是否需要新增 `strptime()` 构造函数，尤其是在现有方法已经能完成类似任务的情况下。
• 新增功能对代码简洁性和向后兼容性的影响。

Time Helper
A lightweight Python library for effortless datetime handling with timezone support. Built for simplicity and flexibility, it provides a comprehensive set of utilities for parsing, converting, and manipulating dates and times.
Key Features:
🌍
Timezone-aware operations
with abbreviation support (e.g., IST, PST, CET)
🔄
Universal datetime parsing
from strings, timestamps, and various formats
📊
Optional pandas/numpy integration
for DataFrame operations
🎯
Simple, intuitive API
with one-line conversions
🐍
Modern Python 3.10+
with full type hints
Installation
Basic Installation
For core datetime functionality without heavy dependencies:
#
Using pip
pip install time-helper
#
Using uv (recommended)
uv add time-helper
With Optional Dependencies
Add pandas and/or numpy support for DataFrame operations and advanced array handling:
#
With pandas support (includes DataFrame/Series datetime operations)
pip install time-helper[pandas]
uv add time-helper[pandas]
#
With numpy support (for numpy datetime64 conversions)
pip install time-helper[numpy]
uv add time-helper[numpy]
#
With both pandas and numpy
pip install time-helper[pandas,numpy]
uv add time-helper[pandas,numpy]

2. **时区操作**：支持通过名称或缩写处理时区，如 IST、PST，并可轻松转换时区。
3. **日期时间操作**：包括时间舍入（按小时、天、周等）和时间差计算。
4. **可选依赖**：支持与 Pandas、NumPy 集成，便于处理 DataFrame 和数组。

安装方式：
- 基础功能：`pip install time-helper`
- 支持 Pandas：`pip install time-helper[pandas]`
- 支持 NumPy：`pip install time-helper[numpy]`

示例：
```python
from time_helper import any_to_datetime, make_aware, round_time

dt = any_to_datetime("2024-03-15 10:30:45")
aware_dt = make_aware("2024-03-15")
rounded = round_time(dt, "H")
```

该库适用于需要灵活处理日期时间的项目，提供简单直观的 API。

data.title: EPA rescinds $20M for clean water in pesticide-contaminated rural California
data.author: tzs
data.article_summary: 文章报道了特朗普政府撤销了拜登政府拨给加州农业区用于提供清洁水的2000万美元资助，该地区长期遭受农药污染，水源中含有高毒性的1,2,3-TCP等致癌物质。这笔资金原本计划帮助约5,500名居民改善饮水质量，尤其是连接受污染的水井至市政供水系统。由于资金被撤，许多居民仍需购买瓶装水度日，生活负担沉重。当地居民如草莓采摘工人Marcela一家每月需花费450美元购买水，且因语言障碍和信息闭塞，部分居民甚至不知水源有毒。环保组织批评此举不公，正努力寻找解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普政府的环境保护局（EPA）取消了一项资助，该资助原本用于支持多样性、公平和包容（DEI）项目，这一决定引发了不同的反应和争议。

不同观点：
• 特朗普政府的立场：环境保护局将该资助称为“浪费的DEI项目”，表明他们认为该项目不必要或无效，可能意在削减他们认为不必要的开支。

• 支持DEI项目者的立场：倡导者认为取消资助是“一种残酷的行为”，暗示此举会损害弱势群体或特定社区的利益，尤其是在多样性、公平和包容方面。

• 当地居民和健康倡导者的关注：评论提到蒙特雷县部分地区的饮用水几十年来一直不安全，受到高度有毒的农药成分污染，这直接威胁到农业工人和其他居民的健康。取消相关资助可能会加剧这些健康风险。

补充讨论：
• 健康与环境问题：评论指出蒙特雷县的饮用水长期受到污染，这不仅仅是政策或资助的问题，更是关系到居民健康和环境保护的紧迫问题。

• 争议焦点：取消资助是否是一种合理的财政紧缩措施，还是对特定群体和健康问题的忽视甚至伤害，成为讨论的核心争议点。

• 政治背景：特朗普政府对DEI项目的立场可能与其整体政策方向有关，反映出对这类项目优先级的不同理解和态度。

44677770.article_content:
Farm workers pick strawberries in the Salinas valley in California.
Photograph: Bob Kreisel/Alamy
View image in fullscreen
Farm workers pick strawberries in the Salinas valley in California.
Photograph: Bob Kreisel/Alamy
California
White House rescinds $20m for clean water in pesticide-contaminated rural California
EPA said grant to provide clean water was a ‘wasteful DEI program’ as pesticide leaches into residents’ wells
Tom Perkins
Thu 24 Jul 2025 07.00 EDT
Last modified on Thu 24 Jul 2025 07.01 EDT
Share
For decades, thousands of residents in
California
’s agricultural heartland couldn’t use their wells because the water was too contaminated with
pesticides
. In December, the
Biden administration
stepped in with a long-awaited $20m grant to provide clean water, improve municipal sources and relieve the region’s financial and health burden.
The
Trump administration
just took the money away.
Donald Trump’s Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) labeled the grant a “wasteful DEI program”, though advocates say the move is an act of cruelty. Drinking water in some parts of the Monterey county region, which largely produces strawberries, has not been safe for decades because it is contaminated with staggering levels of highly toxic pesticide ingredients that threaten the health of agricultural workers and others.
Trump administration yanks $15m in research into Pfas on US farms: ‘not just stupid, it’s evil’
Read more
The decision to yank the money was “unjust”, said Maraid Jimenez, a spokesperson for the Community
Water
Center, which was helping manage the grant’s implementation.
“People agree that everyone needs safe drinking water, so to have a grant help fix that for a rural community rescinded – it doesn’t make any sense to us,” Jimenez said. “The
drinking water crisis here
only gets worse, and, beyond our shock, we’re trying to mobilize to find a solution.”
The funding, along with
California
state money, would have improved drinking water quality for about 5,500 people, either through improvements to municipal infrastructure or by connecting contaminated wells to municipal lines.
The aquifer in the rural, majority-Spanish-speaking communities in Monterey county, which sits about 50 miles (80km) south of the San Jose, is
widely contaminated
with 1,2,3-TCP, a pesticide ingredient and carcinogen banned in 40 countries that persists for decades in the soil and groundwater. In many cases, the 1,2,3-TCP levels in wells have been found to far exceed state limits and EPA health guidelines for drinking water. 1,2,3-TCP can also evaporate and create toxic fumes in the shower, and it is linked to liver, kidney and reproductive damage.
The wells also often contain high levels of arsenic, hexavalent chromium and nitrates. Each are
carcinogens
and the latter can cause “blue baby syndrome”, a condition in young children that causes their skin to turn blue when the toxin gets into their bloodstream and restricts oxygen flow.
Residents have either had to buy jugs of water or use state assistance to purchase them over the last 30 years. Among them is Marcela, a mother of three who has lived in the region for about 10 years. She and her husband are strawberry pickers, and she declined to provide her last name for fear of retaliation from the federal government.
Marcela said the family, which lives near Moss Landing, spends about $450 every three weeks on 5-gallon jugs of water. The well on the property that she rents is broken. She and her landlords, an elderly couple who live at the house and whom she takes care of, don’t have enough money to fix it. Even if they could, the water from the well would in all likelihood be too contaminated to use.
They learned in late 2024 of the plan to connect their property to a nearby water district within three years, which would have alleviated a major stress and financial burden. Then they learned that the
Trump administration
had rescinded the funding.
“It is devastating news for us,” Marcela said via a translator. “We urgently need water.”
Marcela’s family is protected by the bottled water, but some in the region “didn’t know that they couldn’t drink or cook with the tap water, so they would use it”, said Mayra Hernandez, community advocacy manager with Community Water Center. What that has meant for their health is unclear.
Educating residents about the risks has involved Community Water Center staff knocking on doors. The challenges in getting out the word in the region, where there are a large number of workers who don’t speak English and who live in isolation from information sources, highlights how essential it is to hook up properties to clean water.
The EPA grant, along with state funding, would have connected more than 1,000 residents with unsafe wells to municipal lines. It also would have provided financial support to municipal systems needed to expand water provision and provide improvements.
